decisions: Inspected all worker merges, route passages and 32 substantive edits. Separated HSI work assignments and three street practices; removed the unsupported Tolerance camera bridge and isolated custody/Societal relabeling. Local conditional environmental benefits and the attributed surveillance forecast do not require stronger shared votes. Specific harm and allocation bridges remain local.
source_context_read: Bill spending limits and baseline-law passages; HSI reassignment reports and advocacy accounts; Interior/Forest Service observations; GAO scanner constraints; drug replacement and crime null evidence; May 2026 tactics reports; Brennan forecast; warehouse water constraints and injunction. Sources were targeted passages, not a full new evidence review.

merges.decision: The reported reassignment of existing HSI staff is a concrete challenge to this assignment step. The legal spending limit cuts the other way. Reports do not show where new hires would work. Other HSI assignments are separate propositions.

The original arguments claim local or conditional protection, not a net reduction across all wild land. The two historical observations are sourced context; displacement and faster interception remain local inferences rather than one stronger shared test.

Substantive objection: drug-policy researchers argue that traffickers cheaply replace seized fentanyl. This same step carries health and family arguments.
Substantive objection: published studies of similar programs found no measured effect on overall crime or violent victimization. The same step carries three arguments.
Reports of changed tactics bear on this precise continuation premise. Other practices receive separate judgments.

paths.original_excerpt: Section 201's staffing and section 103's surveillance funds support patrols of the kind Interior credits with these local reductions. Where added patrols cut crossings through wild areas, they can reduce this pollution. Protecting wildlife water serves [NAME]'s care for nature.
paths.necessity_reason: Less pollution of wildlife water needs funded patrols that reduce traffic near that water, not only move it.

paths.original_excerpt: Funding staff and faster detection strengthens the ability to stop damaging traffic and fence damage. That protects plants, wildlife habitat, and soil from destruction, which [NAME] values.
paths.necessity_reason: Faster interception protects habitat only if funded surveillance reduces damaging traffic overall.

paths.original_excerpt: Added staffing and surveillance support interception of this traffic. Less unlawful travel through parks and refuges can reduce one route by which harmful species spread there. Reducing such introductions is a way to protect nature.
paths.necessity_reason: Fewer introduced species through this route needs less unlawful travel through parks and refuges.

paths.original_excerpt: Supporting interception before people travel and camp through natural areas strengthens prevention of these ignitions. Avoiding fires that destroy nature gives [NAME] another reason to favor S.2.
paths.necessity_reason: Fewer abandoned campfires needs fewer people traveling and camping in wild areas, not only moved traffic.

paths.original_excerpt: S.2 supports staff who detect fires and bring in the crews needed to control them. This strengthens protection of natural areas from spreading fire.
paths.necessity_reason: The fire-warning benefit reaches S.2 through Section 101 staff.

paths.original_excerpt: S.2 supports the border-enforcement side of this division of work. Preserving land officers' time for protecting natural resources serves [NAME]'s care for nature.
paths.necessity_reason: The argument assigns added immigration work to Section 201 staff.

paths.original_excerpt: Section 101's support for duties outside immigration and customs enforcement backs staff who help secure these work areas. Enabling people to carry out this care for vegetation supports the active defense of nature that [NAME] values.
paths.necessity_reason: The planned-burn benefit reaches S.2 through Section 101 staff.

paths.original_excerpt: S.2 funds equipment used in this work. Strengthening the ability to stop illegal fishing protects marine life and serves [NAME]'s concern for nature.
paths.necessity_reason: The benefit reaches S.2 through Section 103 aircraft and boat money.

paths.original_excerpt: S.2's platform funds add to the fleet whose crews have been called on for this support. The use is occasional and depends on which aircraft are bought, but it can add to the capacity to coordinate pollution cleanup. Helping contain oil pollution serves [NAME]'s aim of protecting nature.
paths.necessity_reason: The benefit reaches S.2 through Section 103 aircraft money.

paths.original_excerpt: Added transport funding supports flights with both kinds of pollution. [NAME]'s wish to protect the environment from pollution gives a reason to oppose that support.
paths.necessity_reason: Flight pollution reaches S.2 through Section 202 transport money.

paths.original_excerpt: S.2 gives ICE more resources to run facilities with this effect. The disturbance at this already-cleared site is small, but protecting wildlife still gives [NAME] a reason to oppose that added support.
paths.necessity_reason: The site effect reaches S.2 through money to keep enforcement facilities running.

paths.original_excerpt: Added money for these facilities and vehicle fleets supports activities that emit air pollution. [NAME]'s wish to prevent pollution gives a reason to oppose it.
paths.necessity_reason: The emissions reach S.2 through facility and vehicle money.

paths.original_excerpt: More operating money supports a detention network pursuing warehouse conversions with documented sewage risks, as Social Circle's plans show. Protecting land, water, and the wildlife that depends on them gives [NAME] a reason to oppose that support.
paths.necessity_reason: Pollution risk needs operating money that adds to the risk from planned warehouse sites.

paths.original_excerpt: Extra money for these patrols supports off-road driving that damages soil, plants, and habitat. Protecting wild places gives [NAME] a reason to oppose it.
paths.necessity_reason: The patrol harm reaches S.2 through Section 201 staffing money.

paths.original_excerpt: More capacity to arrest and remove these workers puts time-sensitive forest care at risk. Protecting forests gives [NAME] a reason to oppose that added capacity.
paths.necessity_reason: The risk to crews reaches S.2 through enforcement staff money in both sections.

paths.original_excerpt: S.2's platform money can enlarge or upgrade the aerial fleet whose drones have been lent for monitoring environmental defenders, although the bill does not specify drones. The added risk of deterring their participation gives [NAME], who values taking part in defending nature, a reason to oppose it.
paths.necessity_reason: The drone concern reaches S.2 only through Section 103 platform money.

paths.necessity_reason: Family teaching is protected only if added scanning is used and reduces the drugs reaching people.

paths.original_excerpt: Living apart disrupts shared family life and parents' daily teaching. Preserving these family duties gives [NAME] a reason to oppose the added funding.
paths.necessity_reason: Family teaching is threatened through added removal money and family separation.

paths.original_excerpt: Adding resources to enforcement that already keeps people from church puts shared worship, teaching and rites under greater pressure. [NAME] has a reason to oppose that threat to practicing and passing on the faith.
paths.necessity_reason: Local route: the threat to worship is specific to this argument.

paths.original_excerpt: Added removal capacity puts congregations' leaders and membership at greater risk. Losing a congregation breaks the continuity of a community that carries Christian teaching, worship and customs. Preserving that community gives [NAME] a reason to oppose S.2.
paths.necessity_reason: The threat to congregations reaches S.2 through removal money.

paths.original_excerpt: More resources for operations that have interrupted this church's ministry increase the risk of further interruptions to its continuing communal religious work. Maintaining that established ministry, rather than endorsing care for strangers in the abstract, supplies [NAME]'s Tradition reason.
paths.necessity_reason: Local route: the interrupted ministry is specific to this argument.

paths.original_excerpt: Supporting more custody exposes more Christians and their pastors to these access barriers. [NAME] has a reason to oppose that risk to prayer, pastoral care and an inherited duty of the church.
paths.necessity_reason: Access barriers reach S.2 through added custody.

paths.original_excerpt: Additional removal capacity supports a system that has returned Christians to danger and puts accompanying relatives' worship at risk. Preserving their freedom to live by their faith gives [NAME] a reason to oppose S.2.
paths.necessity_reason: The danger reaches S.2 through removal money.
